wiki-guide.title: How to Use Eryndor Wiki
wiki-guide.summary: Find information, player commands, favorites and automatic content updates.
wiki-guide.search: wiki guide search offline updates commands favorites encyclopedia
wiki-guide.content:
Eryndor Wiki is an encyclopedia of the Pixelmon server's rules. Here you can find explanations of game mechanics, useful commands, related guides and information about the world of Eryndor.

Searching

Enter the name of a mechanic, item or command in the search field at the top of the screen. You can also use categories to narrow the results.

Favorites and commands

Tap the star beside an article to add it to the favorites saved on your phone. If an article contains a useful player command, use the Copy button.

Updates and offline access

When you open the Wiki, the app checks whether new articles are available. Downloaded content stays on your phone, so you can read it later without an internet connection. Content updates do not require you to install a new APK.

You can find the last updated date beside each article. Use the “Files” tab to download shared resources.

Related articles

fishing.title: Pixelmon Fishing
fishing.summary: The fishing rod from Khar-Durim's harbor, fishing rules, the minigame and a spoiler-free Fish Atlas.
fishing.search: fishing fish atlas minigame lava water End Nether catches treasures bonuses odds
fishing.content:
Pixelmon Fishing adds 58 unique fish species, a special fishing rod, a skill-based minigame, treasures and a Fish Atlas. It is a separate activity from catching Pokémon with a regular fishing rod.

Where do I get the fishing rod?

The special Pixelmon Fishing rod will be available for purchase from an NPC in the harbor of Khar-Durim. It is used to catch fish from this system, not Pokémon.

Where and how can I fish?

  • Use the dedicated Pixelmon Fishing rod near a suitable body of liquid. It must have a surface of at least 3×3 blocks and a depth of 2 blocks.
  • Overworld: fish in water, often depending on the biome.
  • Nether: fish in lava anywhere in the dimension.
  • End: fish in water.
  • Lava in the Overworld and End is not supported by this activity and will not start a fishing attempt.

How does the minigame work?

Cast your line, wait for a bite and hook the fish. After a moment, a vertical minigame appears. Hold the right mouse button to raise the green zone; release it to let the zone fall. Try to keep the moving fish inside the green zone.

  • The progress bar starts at approximately 25%.
  • Reaching 100% means a successful catch; falling to 0% means failure.
  • Fish have different movement patterns and three difficulty levels: easy, hard and very hard.
  • Whether you hooked a fish, junk or treasure is decided before the minigame, but you still need to win to claim the catch.

What can you catch?

In addition to fish of varying rarity, you may catch treasure or unwanted items. Different specimens are available in different places, and certain dishes can affect your fishing experience.

Fish Atlas — discovering species

There are 58 species to discover on your own in the Fish Atlas. Find new specimens by fishing under suitable conditions. Each successful discovery adds to your collection, while entries for fish you have not seen remain hidden.

You can find information about discovered species and track your collection in the Atlas. Explore and fish to uncover new entries yourself.

/fish atlasOpens the Fish Atlas, showing discovered species and collection progress.

Fishing rewards and completing the Atlas

Discovering the entire collection unlocks a special Fisher aura. Daily Quests may offer a “Catch 20 fish” task worth 4,500 ₽. Successful Pixelmon Fishing catches count toward this quest; junk and treasure do not.

Cooking bonuses

Some Pixelmon Cooking dishes make fishing easier. Look up the effects of discovered dishes in the Culinary Atlas.

mushrooms.title: Mushroom Foraging
mushrooms.summary: Mushroom gathering, a spoiler-free Atlas, artifacts, and trading and selling through an NPC.
mushrooms.search: mushroom foraging atlas mushrooms basket medallion alchemist NPC selling trading EXP Candy
mushrooms.content:
Mushroom Foraging is a system for finding and gathering unique mushrooms scattered throughout different areas of Eryndor. Mushrooms can be sold, traded for EXP Candy, used in Cooking or collected in the Atlas.

How do I find and gather mushrooms?

Mushrooms appear in designated zones, not randomly throughout the entire world. When you find an active mushroom, you can gather it to obtain an item and record a discovery in your Atlas. Rarity and location affect what you might find. Once an area has been cleared, mushrooms respawn according to server settings.

Mushroom Forager's Atlas

There are 27 mushroom species to discover. Personally gathering a new specimen reveals its Atlas entry, which also tracks your collection progress and the number of mushrooms gathered. Undiscovered entries remain a mystery.

Searching for new specimens is part of the adventure. The Atlas lets you track your collection and learn more about mushrooms you have already discovered.

/mushroom atlasOpens the Mushroom Forager's Atlas and shows discovery progress.

Selling and trading mushrooms — special NPC

You will be able to sell and trade mushrooms with the Alchemist. The NPC opens a trading screen, so you do not need to use any commands.

RarityDefault price per item
Common200 ₽
Uncommon750 ₽
Legendary4,000 ₽

Check the current prices with the Alchemist.

Alchemist — trading for EXP Candy

In the Alchemist's trading system, mushrooms may be counted by rarity rather than by their individual species names. The NPC interface shows the exact requirements and rewards on offer.

RewardCommonUncommonLegendary
EXP Candy S500
EXP Candy M1020
EXP Candy L1260
EXP Candy XL10101

You trade with the Alchemist through the NPC's interface, not through a command.

Two Mushroom Forager artifacts

  • Medalion Grzybiarza (Forager's Medallion): while carried in your inventory, it warns you when an active mushroom is nearby. Its range is up to 24 blocks, but it does not reveal the direction, species or exact distance. Notifications have a cooldown.
  • Koszyk Grzybiarza (Forager's Basket): while carried in your inventory, subtle particles point toward nearby active mushrooms. Its range is 12 blocks. Only the owner sees the effect.

Cooking, quests and completing the Atlas

Forager's Stew from Pixelmon Cooking gives a 25% chance of receiving an extra mushroom for 15 minutes. This bonus does not double Atlas discoveries or daily quest progress.

After you discover all 27 species, the server announces the completion of your Atlas. Any additional rewards depend on the world's settings.

daily-quests.title: Daily Quests
daily-quests.summary: Three quests per day, reset times, progress tracking and activity rewards on Eryndor.
daily-quests.search: daily quests tasks three per day midnight reset rewards catching battling mining fishing casino
daily-quests.content:
Daily Quests is a system of daily tasks that lets you earn Pokédollars while enjoying normal gameplay. Tasks include catching and defeating Pokémon, gathering resources, mushroom foraging, fishing, cooking, evolution, breeding and Casino 777.

How many quests do I get each day?

  • Every player receives 3 quests per day.
  • Quests cover different activities. You will not receive the exact same task two days in a row.
  • A new set appears at 00:00 server time. Unfinished quests do not automatically carry over into the next day.
  • After completing a task, click “Claim” in the GUI to collect your reward.

How do I use the quest board?

The board shows 3 scrolls containing quests. Each displays the description, progress, reward and claim option. When you complete a quest, you receive a chat notification. Make sure to claim rewards before the daily reset.

Pokémon — catching, battling and training

Example questReward
Catch 10 Pokémon of the specified type5,000 ₽
Catch 30 Pokémon4,000 ₽
Defeat 25 Pokémon of the specified type5,500 ₽
Defeat 50 Pokémon4,500 ₽
Evolve 5 Pokémon4,500 ₽
Fish up 15 Pokémon2,500 ₽
Complete 2 breeding sessions5,000 ₽

Dual-type Pokémon also count toward type-specific tasks if one of their types matches. The type specified in your current quest always determines progress.

Gathering, cooking and fishing

QuestReward
Gather 40 mushrooms3,000 ₽
Catch 20 Pixelmon Fishing fish4,500 ₽
Cook 5 different dishesReward shown in the GUI

For the “5 different dishes” quest, cooking the same dish repeatedly does not advance progress: the system checks for different dish types. The fishing quest counts custom fish, not junk or treasures from the minigame.

Mining ores

QuestReward
Mine 25 coal ore3,000 ₽
Mine 15 iron ore3,500 ₽
Mine 10 gold ore4,000 ₽
Mine 15 copper ore3,000 ₽

The verified mining quests also count the corresponding deepslate ores.

Casino 777

QuestReward
Spin the slot machine 10 times15,000 ₽
Play 5 rounds of blackjack7,500 ₽

Progress requires actually playing the games; merely entering the casino does not count.

Making the most of your day

Check all three quests before you start playing so you can combine activities. If you receive fishing and cooking quests, catch the ingredients first and then use them in the cauldron. For mining and mushroom quests, plan a route through the appropriate zones.

The quest board shows your currently assigned tasks and rewards.

bingo.title: Bingo
bingo.summary: Bingo 4×4, money rewards, Common/Exceptional/Epic Crate keys and a daily board.
bingo.search: bingo 4x4 board Pokemon 24 hours reset rows columns rewards crate keys common crate exceptional crate epic crate zwykła skrzynia wyjątkowa skrzynia epicka skrzynia
bingo.content:
Bingo is a fully implemented daily collecting challenge based on catching Pokémon. Each board has a 4×4 grid, with 16 spaces to fill.

How do I play?

  1. Open your Bingo board in the game. It shows which Pokémon you need for the challenge.
  2. Catch Pokémon that match the entries on your current card.
  3. Fill the spaces and try to complete rows, columns or the entire board according to the in-game reward rules.
  4. Once you have completed your current board, wait for a new daily card.

Board and reset

Bingo operates on a 24-hour cycle. Your board shows the current objectives and your progress toward them.

Rewards

You can earn monetary rewards worth 500 ₽, 1,500 ₽ and 5,000 ₽, depending on the type of achievement on the board. The current Bingo configuration displays the exact thresholds and available rewards.

Progress on your board also awards keys to the Common, Exceptional and Epic Crates:

CompletionKey
Each newly completed spaceCommon Crate (Zwykła Skrzynia) — 1 key
Each completed row or columnExceptional Crate (Wyjątkowa Skrzynia) — 1 key
Entire 4×4 boardEpic Crate (Epicka Skrzynia) — 1 key

You can complete at most 16 spaces, 8 lines and one full board on a single card. Crate contents are randomized: receiving a key does not guarantee any particular item.

What does the GUI show?

  • Your 4×4 card, with Pokémon and each space's status.
  • Information about completed spaces, without unnecessary repetition of instructions.
  • A scrollable spawn list to help you find Pokémon.
  • Completed entry indicators and a clear division of information.

casino.title: Casino 777 and Token Shop
casino.summary: The 777 slot machine, blackjack, Jade Orbs, Casino Tokens and CoinToShop rewards.
casino.search: casino 777 blackjack jade orb casino token cointoshop slot machine
casino.content:
Casino 777 is a completed Eryndor attraction where you can play a slot machine or blackjack. You can win Żetony Kasyna (Casino Tokens), which are then spent in a special NPC-run shop.

777 Slot Machine

One spin costs 3 Jade Orbs. One Jade Orb is worth 500 ₽, so the total price is 1,500 ₽ per spin. The machine rolls a result and awards the appropriate number of tokens if you land a winning combination.

The number of tokens and the probability of specific symbols depend on the machine's rules. A spin is not a guaranteed profit.

Blackjack

One round of blackjack costs 1 Jade Orb (500 ₽). Your goal is to get closer to 21 than the dealer without going over 21, following the rules of the available minigame.

ResultReward
Regular win2 Casino Tokens
Blackjack (natural 21)3 Casino Tokens

Tokens and the Casino Shop

Żetony Kasyna (Casino Tokens) have their own icon and can be exchanged for rewards in CoinToShop. The shop has 4 item categories, and some prizes cost up to 2,300 tokens.

Open the shop by interacting with the appropriate NPC; you do not need to remember a command. Opening the shop with a keyboard shortcut is disabled.

Related Daily Quests

Casino activities may appear in Daily Quests: 10 slot spins is a task worth 15,000 ₽, while 5 blackjack rounds reward 7,500 ₽. Progress is based on games actually played.

Things to remember

  • Jade Orbs are the cost of playing, while Casino Tokens are a separate reward currency.
  • Do not expect automatic compensation after several losses. Only spend the currency you want to put toward this attraction.
  • Shop prices and available items may change with server balance adjustments. Check the NPC for the current selection.

identity.title: Eryndor Identity
identity.summary: Title Scrolls, your collection, title selection, colors, duplicates and chat appearance.
identity.search: Eryndor Identity titles scroll chat nickname color duplicates selling collection
identity.content:
Eryndor Identity lets you collect and display player titles. Obtain scrolls, unlock their associated titles, then select one to show alongside your name in chat. Titles are collectible and cosmetic; they do not improve your Pokémon's stats.

How do I obtain and unlock a title?

  1. Collect Zwoje Tytułów (Title Scrolls) as rewards from different server activities or obtain them from other players.
  2. Hold a scroll and hold down the right mouse button for approximately 1.5 seconds. A quick click is not enough.
  3. Using the scroll correctly adds its title to your collection and consumes one scroll from your inventory.
  4. Open the Identity menu and choose the title you want to use.

Unlocking a title is permanent: your collection and active selection remain saved even after logging out or restarting the server.

What if I get the same scroll again?

If you already have the title associated with a scroll, the game tells you it is a duplicate. The scroll is not consumed. You may keep it or give it to another player.

Duplicate value: from 5,000 ₽ to 15,000 ₽, depending on the title.

Title list and selecting an active title

In the Identity window you can scroll through the entire title list. Unlocked titles are highlighted and displayed at the top; locked titles are grayed out. Select an unlocked title and press “Set”. You may have only one active title at a time. The “Remove active” button hides your current title without taking away your ability to use it again.

/identityOpens the title panel. The /titles command opens the same panel.
/identity listShows your owned titles and the title currently selected.
/identity offDisables your active title without removing it from your collection.

How do titles appear in chat?

Messages follow the format Title | Nickname: message, without additional brackets. Player names remain green, while titles retain their own color, gradient and any decorative symbols. For example: ♠ Pokerzysta ♠ | Nickname: Hello!

Players without an active title chat normally: Nickname: message. Subtle separators divide message blocks without splitting longer messages that wrap across multiple lines.

Title appearances

Some titles have unusual visual effects: unique colors, gradients, symbols or changing color schemes. These do not affect how chat works or your combat abilities. Titles come from different Eryndor reward sources; discovering them is part of the collection experience.

Each title is unlocked using its corresponding Title Scroll. Track your collection through the Identity menu.

mastery.title: Eryndor Mastery
mastery.summary: Complete guide to levels 100–105, ranks M1–M5, battles, expeditions, palette discounts, auras and commands.
mastery.search: mastery levels 100 101 102 103 104 105 battle horde faint capture palette discount M1 M2 M3 M4 M5 expedition aura PC /mastery particles
mastery.content:
Eryndor Mastery lets you train Pokémon beyond the usual level 100 cap, all the way up to level 105. Each Pokémon has its own Mastery ranks, from M1 through M5. To reach the next rank, that Pokémon must meet the stage's requirements by completing qualifying battles and expeditions.

When does Mastery begin?

Mastery progression becomes available only at level 100. Battles and expeditions completed before then do not count toward Mastery. Simply reaching level 100 does not grant M1; it only unlocks the opportunity to begin the first stage.

Later stages also have minimum Pokémon level requirements. For example, a Pokémon must already be level 101 to start progressing toward M2. Likewise, M3 requires level 102, M4 requires 103, and M5 requires 104.

Mastery requirements table

Rank to earnMinimum levelBattlesExpeditionsUnlocked level cap
M11002002Level 101
M21013003Level 102
M31024004Level 103
M41035005Level 104
M51047506Level 105

Important: the numbers in this table apply separately to each rank. They are not cumulative totals across M0–M5. After earning a rank, the counters for that stage reset to zero. The next rank's requirements are independent of the previous ones.

Which battles count?

A battle victory (or successfully catching the opposing Pokémon) counts only for Pokémon that meet all of these conditions:

  • The Pokémon must participate in the battle.
  • It must use at least one move. Merely entering the battlefield is not enough.
  • It must not faint at any point during the battle. Reviving it later does not change this: the battle will not count for that Pokémon.
  • The player must win. A draw, escape, surrender or improperly ended battle does not award progress.
  • A horde battle counts as one battle, even when it involves multiple opponents.
  • The Pokémon must already meet the level requirement for its current Mastery stage.

If several of your Pokémon use a move in the same winning battle and none of them faints, each eligible Pokémon can receive its own credit. However, defeating several opponents during a single battle does not award multiple credits to one Pokémon.

Catching Pokémon

Successfully catching an opposing Pokémon may be treated as winning the battle and count toward Mastery. Participation requirements still apply: your Pokémon must have used a move and must not have fainted earlier. Throwing a Poké Ball alone does not replace the required Pokémon move.

How do expeditions count?

An expedition can award Mastery progress when the trip finishes, even if you have not claimed the reward yet. Claiming rewards is not required when the completion has already been recorded. Sending a party out or having an expedition still in progress does not count.

If an expedition finishes while you are away from the server, check your Mastery progress after logging in again.

  • The Pokémon sent on the expedition receives progress if its current Mastery stage is active.
  • It must meet the level requirement for that rank (100 for M1 and 101–104 for subsequent stages).
  • Each completed expedition can count at most once for that Pokémon; repeatedly checking its status or collecting the reward does not award additional credits.
  • An expedition completed before a Mastery stage becomes active is not banked for later.

To earn each rank, you must complete both types of requirement: battles and expeditions. One cannot replace the other.

Special palette discount

A Pokémon with a non-default palette receives a 10% discount on the number of battles required for its next Mastery rank. This discount does not reduce the required number of expeditions or the minimum level.

RankDefault paletteSpecial paletteExpeditions
M12001802
M23002703
M34003604
M45004505
M57506756

Note: the battle threshold for a stage is determined when you earn the first qualifying battle credit for that stage. Changing the palette after that will not alter the threshold for the same rank. The threshold can be calculated again when beginning a new stage.

Ranking up and leveling

When a Pokémon completes both requirements, it automatically advances to the next Mastery rank. A confirmation appears in chat, and you receive a message about the newly earned rank.

Mastery advancement increases the permitted level cap; it does not immediately grant the Pokémon a free level. You must still earn experience or use an available leveling method. For example, after earning M1, a level 100 Pokémon can reach level 101. Only after reaching level 101 does it begin making progress toward M2.

When a Pokémon reaches its currently unlocked level cap, earning more experience or using Rare Candy to gain another level is blocked until the next Mastery advancement.

Auras and PC badges

Pokémon with ranks M1–M4 have subtle golden-white sparks. Rank M5 adds more elaborate effects and lets you select a color: gold, blue, purple, green or red.

Auras appear around Pokémon sent out into the world, except while they are battling. Each player can turn the Mastery particle display on or off in the GUI settings. Disabling it changes only what you personally see; it does not remove auras for other players.

In Pixelmon's standard PC, Pokémon also have small M1–M5 badges, including in the party bar at the bottom. These make trained Pokémon easy to recognize without opening their details.

Practical example

You have a level 100 Pokémon with its default palette. You win 200 qualifying battles with it and send it on two expeditions that are completed. The Pokémon reaches M1, raising its level cap to 101.

You then reach level 101. Only now does the M2 stage begin, requiring another 300 battles and 3 completed expeditions. If the Pokémon has a special palette from the beginning of that stage, 270 battles are enough instead of 300.

Useful commands

/masteryOpens the Mastery GUI for your party, including progress, requirements and aura settings.
/mastery 1Opens Mastery details for the Pokémon in your first party slot. You can specify slot numbers 1–6.
/mastery particles offHides Mastery particles in your view. To restore them, use /mastery particles on.

You can also select the M5 aura color directly in the Mastery GUI without memorizing another command.

cooking.title: Pixelmon Cooking
cooking.summary: Cauldron cooking, 29 dishes and vitamins, their effects and an Atlas of hidden recipes.
cooking.search: cooking dishes soup stew feast broth vitamins Speed Haste catch rate catch combo exp breeding egg steps fishing mushroom atlas cauldron
cooking.content:
Pixelmon Cooking lets you prepare dishes using unique fish, mushrooms and regular Minecraft ingredients. Food can restore hunger, give the player helpful effects, improve fishing and Pokémon catching, increase experience gain or assist with breeding.

Kociołek Kulinarny and required materials

To craft the cauldron, place 2 copper ingots in the top corners, 4 iron ingots in the middle and bottom corners, and 1 block of iron in the center of the bottom row.

Place it above a heat source: fire, soul fire, a lit campfire, a lit soul campfire or lava. An extinguished campfire will not work. The cauldron has five ingredient slots and a separate slot for the finished dish.

Kociołek Kulinarny — 3×3 crafting recipe

Arrange the ingredients as shown to craft the Kociołek Kulinarny:

@@COOKING_IMAGE@@

C—C
I—I
IBI

Key: C = copper ingot, I = iron ingot, B = block of iron.

How to cook

  • Add 3–5 different permitted ingredients; the order does not matter. Each dish requires its particular combination of ingredients.
  • You cannot substitute repeated copies of the same item for several different ingredients.
  • The GUI shows the heating status, remaining time and expected result. Undiscovered recipes remain hidden as ???.
  • Dishes take 10 to 60 seconds to cook, depending on the recipe.
  • A permitted but unrecognized ingredient combination produces Zatruty Gulasz after a random 10–30 seconds. An ingredient that is not permitted prevents cooking entirely.
  • Finished dishes of the same kind can stack up to 64, and the cauldron continues cooking as long as there are ingredients and room for the output.

Culinary Atlas

There are 29 recipes to discover. The Atlas displays the combinations you have found, their ingredients, cooking times and dish effects. Zatruty Gulasz does not have an Atlas entry. You can accidentally make it, but it does not count toward completing the book.

/cooking atlasOpens the Culinary Atlas and shows your recipe discovery progress.

Dishes and their effects

Every dish has its own properties. The tables below list dish names, effects and durations. Discover which ingredients are required for each dish yourself through the Culinary Atlas.

Minecraft effects

DishEffectDuration
Lekka Zupa GońcaSpeed I — increases movement speed20 min
Uczta GońcaSpeed II — greater movement speed increase10 min
Gulasz KamieniarzaHaste I — speeds up mining25 min
Gulasz GórnikaHaste II — greater mining speed increase15 min
Bulion NurkaWater Breathing — allows breathing underwater30 min
Zupa Nocnego WędrowcaNight Vision — helps you see in darkness30 min
Skoczna PotrawkaJump Boost I — lets you jump higher5 min
Morska PotrawkaDolphin’s Grace — increases swimming speed30 min

Effects such as Speed, Haste and Night Vision can be active simultaneously, even when they come from different dishes.

Special bonuses

DishEffectDuration
Zupa RybakaIncreases the green zone in the Fishing minigame by 50%15 min
Klarowny Bulion WędkarzaEliminates junk catches during Fishing15 min

Gulasz GrzybiarzaGives a 25% chance of receiving an additional mushroom when gathering15 min
Lekka Uczta TreneraIncreases Pokémon experience gain by 15%10 min
Królewska Uczta TreneraIncreases Pokémon experience gain by 25%10 min

Kociołek Mistrza ŁowówCatch Rate +30% when catching Pokémon5 min
Potrawka Łowcy SeriiIncreases Catch Combo gains to +2 instead of +115 min

You can have only one special Cooking bonus active at a time. Eating another dish with a special bonus replaces the previous one. This restriction does not apply to regular Minecraft effects.

Dishes for breeders

DishEffectRestrictions
Gulasz HodowcyReduces the time of the next Pokémon breeding session by 30%One-time use; can be used again after 2 hours
Jajeczna Potrawka HodowcyReduces the remaining steps required to hatch eggs in your party by 50%One-time use; requires an egg in the party; can be used again after 2 hours

Breeding dish cooldown: 2 hours. Gulasz Hodowcy and Jajeczna Potrawka Hodowcy have separate cooldowns. After using one of these dishes, you cannot use the same dish again until two hours have elapsed.

The egg-step reducing dish affects eggs that are already in your active party.

Filling meals

DishEffect
Wiejska PotrawkaRestores a large amount of hunger and saturation
Mięsny KociołekRestores a very large amount of hunger and saturation

Pokémon vitamins

The Kociołek Kulinarny can also prepare vitamins that raise a Pokémon's corresponding Effort Values (EVs).

VitaminStat
HP UpHP EVs
ProteinAttack EVs
IronDefense EVs
CalciumSpecial Attack EVs

CarbosSpeed EVs

Failed cooking

An unrecognized combination of permitted ingredients can produce Zatruty Gulasz, which inflicts Poison, Nausea and Hunger II. This dish does not count toward the Atlas's 29 discoveries.

backpacks.title: Sophisticated Backpacks
backpacks.summary: Backpacks, upgrades and verified crafting recipes, including two ways to make an Iron Backpack.
backpacks.search: sophisticated backpacks leather string chest copper iron gold diamond netherite magnet stack pickup upgrade
backpacks.content:
Sophisticated Backpacks adds backpacks that provide extra item storage and a comprehensive upgrade system. You can carry a backpack, place it in the world, change its colors and customize it to suit your playstyle.

Your first backpack

Craft a basic Backpack with 4 String, 4 Leather and 1 wooden Chest.

Basic Backpack — 3×3 crafting recipe

Place the items in the exact positions shown on the crafting table. The recipe produces one basic backpack.

@@BACKPACK_CARD:backpack@@

Using a backpack

  • Storage: open your backpack and move items just as you would with a regular chest.
  • Convenient access: assign or check the Open Backpack key in Minecraft's controls. Change the binding there if it conflicts with another mod.
  • Placing: a backpack can also function as a block. Once placed, right-click it to open its inventory.
  • Wearing: a backpack can be equipped and displayed on your character when the active equipment-slot configuration supports it.
  • Colors: use dyes to change your backpack's appearance and distinguish between sets of stored items.

Storage tiers

The available tiers are basic (leather), copper, iron, gold, diamond and netherite. Each higher tier offers more storage space and upgrade options. Upgrading an existing backpack preserves its contents.

Upgrading to Copper Backpack

Surround a basic backpack with 8 Copper Ingots.

@@BACKPACK_CARD:copper_backpack@@

Upgrading to Iron Backpack

There are two ways to obtain an Iron Backpack:

  • From a basic backpack: surround a basic backpack with 8 Iron Ingots.
  • From a Copper Backpack: arrange a Copper Backpack and 4 Iron Ingots above, below, to its left and to its right.

Here is the recipe that upgrades directly from a basic backpack:

@@BACKPACK_CARD:iron_backpack@@

If you already have a Copper Backpack, the upgrade requires only 4 Iron Ingots:

@@BACKPACK_CARD:iron_backpack_from_copper@@

Gold Backpack

Surround an Iron Backpack with 8 Gold Ingots in a 3×3 crafting table.

@@BACKPACK_CARD:gold_backpack@@

Diamond Backpack

Surround a Gold Backpack with 8 Diamonds in a 3×3 crafting table.

@@BACKPACK_CARD:diamond_backpack@@

Netherite Backpack — Smithing Table

In a Smithing Table, combine a Netherite Upgrade Smithing Template, a Diamond Backpack and 1 Netherite Ingot, in that order. This is not a 3×3 crafting recipe, and you do not need to surround a backpack with eight Netherite Ingots.

@@BACKPACK_CARD:netherite_backpack@@

Upgrades worth knowing

  • Pickup / Magnet: help automatically collect items into your backpack.
  • Stack Upgrade: allows larger stacks of items in occupied slots.
  • Crafting: adds a crafting grid inside the backpack.
  • Deposit / Restock: help transfer items or restock supplies.
  • Feeding: allows automatic use of food.
  • Filter: controls which items automation can process.
  • Void: can permanently destroy specified items. Configure its filters very carefully.

Practical tips

A filter and Pickup upgrade can be useful for mining trips; larger capacity is helpful for long exploration sessions; and Stack Upgrades work well with large material collections. After changing upgrades, inspect their settings in the backpack interface; many have their own filters and switches.

If a recipe does not work, check its arrangement in the in-game recipe viewer.

waystones.title: Waystones
waystones.summary: Complete guide to teleportation stones, colored networks, plates, scrolls, shards and 11 Waystones crafting recipes.
waystones.search: waystones waystone warp stone warp dust dormant shard attuned shard crumbling attuned shard deepslate shard warp plate warp portal sharestone portstone blank scroll bound scroll return scroll warp scroll portal scroll twinbound feather epitaph fleeting memorial teleport network crafting
waystones.content:
Waystones lets you activate magical teleportation stones and travel between locations you have discovered. Instead of repeatedly walking long distances, you can return to places you have previously activated.

How do I use a Waystone?

  1. Find a Waystone and right-click it to activate it.
  2. When you interact with an already activated Waystone, open the list of destinations available to you.
  3. Choose a destination and confirm the teleport. Any experience costs or restrictions are displayed in the interface.

A Waystone may be accessible to one player, a team or everyone, depending on the block and server settings. Not every stone you encounter is automatically available without first activating it.

Types of stones and devices

Waystone — teleportation stone

A basic fast-travel point. Once discovered, activate it with a right-click; during later interactions, select an available teleport destination. A Waystone placed by a player is immediately activated for the player who placed it. Its owner may be able to access additional settings when server permissions allow this.

Waystones also come in mossy, sandy, deepslate, blackstone, end stone, red nether brick, purpur, prismarine and mud brick variants. Only their appearance and materials change, not the underlying teleportation mechanic. You do not need to learn a separate set of rules for each variant.

Sharestone — a shared network of one color

Sharestones form networks linked by color. When using one, you can select another Sharestone of the same color. For example, a red Sharestone connects to other red ones, not blue ones. Unlike standard Waystones, this network does not require you to personally discover every destination. The mod offers 15 Sharestone colors — there is no white Sharestone.

Portstone — departure point, not a destination

A Portstone allows teleportation from itself to other points, but it cannot be selected as a teleport destination. A colored Portstone provides access to the Sharestone network of the same color. The White Portstone is an exception: it uses the standard Waystone network. Do not confuse Portstones with Sharestones; they serve different functions.

Warp Plate — automatic teleportation plate

This flat plate teleports a character or permitted entity when they step onto its surface. To send them to a particular location, it needs a shard attuned to the destination plate. When placed, a plate can attune a Dormant Shard, producing a shard that identifies that particular plate. Move the resulting shard to a different Warp Plate to create a link toward the original plate.

Right-click to open the plate's settings; Shift + right-click with an empty hand to remove an inserted shard. A plate can hold several shards and choose between multiple destinations. Special add-ons can change its behavior, including cycling through destinations, teleport timing and response to redstone signals. If there is no valid destination or teleportation is blocked, the plate will not transport the player.

Warp Portal — temporary portal

A portal created using a Portal Scroll. After selecting a destination, a passage appears that can be used by entering it. It requires enough free space to spawn and may stop working when its lifetime expires or its destination becomes unavailable. Unlike a Waystone, it is not an ordinary block you can craft and place directly.

Fleeting Memorial — temporary monument

This monument can appear through the effect of an Epitaph when a player dies, provided there is enough nearby space for it to form. It serves as a single-use return point to the place of death and disappears after a successful teleport to it. It is not a normal building block for a Waystone network.

Teleportation items and scrolls

  • Warp Stone: a portable, reusable item that opens the list of available teleport destinations. Traveling may consume durability, depending on the server configuration. It is not the same as a stationary Waystone.
  • Blank Scroll: an empty scroll. Right-click your chosen Waystone with it to turn it into a Bound Scroll linked to that location.
  • Bound Scroll: a scroll bound to one specific Waystone. Using it teleports you without choosing from a destination list; the scroll is consumed after a successful teleport.
  • Return Scroll: a single-use return scroll. It usually teleports you to the nearest available Waystone. After a journey through a Warp Portal, it may first direct you to that portal's return point, if the point still exists.
  • Warp Scroll: a single-use scroll that opens the list of available destinations and allows you to choose where to teleport.
  • Portal Scroll: does not immediately teleport you. It opens a destination selector and then creates a nearby Warp Portal that players can enter. It requires a sufficiently large area of free space.
  • Twinbound Feather: a magical feather used to link two players. Both players hold their own feather, stand close together and hold right-click while aiming at one another. Once linked, they may gain the ability to teleport to the other's current location while that player is online and still has the linked feather. Server teleport restrictions still apply.
  • Epitaph: an item that can provide a way back to your place of death. When held in your inventory, it may be automatically consumed on death to create a temporary Fleeting Memorial. If the monument cannot be placed, it will not appear.

When using most scrolls, Warp Stones and similar travel items, you hold the right mouse button until activation finishes. Some open a destination selector, while others use an already saved location. Activation time depends on game settings.

Shards and materials

  • Warp Dust: a crafting material for Waystones and Warp Plates. It does not teleport players by itself. Combining an Ender Pearl and an Amethyst Shard yields four portions.
  • Dormant Shard: an inactive shard. When inserted into a Warp Plate, it becomes attuned to that plate after a while, turning into an Attuned Shard.
  • Attuned Shard: a shard that remembers a specific plate. When placed in another Warp Plate, it sets that plate's destination. It can be reused as long as the linked destination remains available.
  • Crumbling Attuned Shard: a single-use version of the Attuned Shard. It may be consumed after a successful teleport through the plate.
  • Deepslate Shard: a special shard that disables a Warp Plate instead of setting a teleport destination. It can be made with deepslate and flint.

Important practical differences

  • Want to return to previously discovered locations? Use a Waystone, Warp Stone or Warp Scroll.
  • Want to create a shared network of colored teleport points? Use Sharestones. A Portstone provides an entry point to that network but is not itself a possible destination.
  • Want to teleport by stepping onto a plate? Link Warp Plates with attuned shards.
  • Want to open a passage for nearby players? Use a Portal Scroll.
  • Want to return after dying? An Epitaph can help, provided its monument can be placed.

Waystones crafting recipes — Minecraft 1.21.1

The following recipes have been verified for Waystones NeoForge 21.1.45. Each illustration shows the exact ingredient layout and output quantity. Shapeless recipes allow ingredients to be arranged in any order.

Teleportation costs and restrictions

Waystones supports configurable experience costs, cooldowns and rules for traveling between dimensions. Check the cost and available options in the game before teleporting.

Tips

  • Activate any Waystones you find before leaving an area.
  • Bring spare scrolls or a Warp Stone on important journeys.
  • Remember that some locations and dimensions may have their own access restrictions based on server progression.

expeditions.title: Eryndor Expeditions
expeditions.summary: 12 expeditions lasting 4/8/16 hours, Expedition Strength, team requirements, Mastery and valuable rewards.
expeditions.search: expeditions missions guild NPC 4h 8h 16h PC pokemon shiny types IV EV SE expedition strength talisman relic rewards titles cosmetics auras mega stones mastery /checkse
expeditions.content:
Eryndor Expeditions lets you send Pokémon on expeditions across Eryndor. Each expedition has its own duration, team requirements and reward pool. A stronger team may return with more items and a better chance of finding exceptional treasures.

There are 12 expeditions available: four each lasting 4, 8 or 16 hours.

How to start an expedition

  1. Visit the Expeditions NPC and open the expedition menu.
  2. Choose an expedition and review its requirements, duration and possible rewards.
  3. Select suitable Pokémon from your PC.
  4. Make sure your team meets every requirement, then confirm the expedition.
Important: Pokémon sent on an expedition are temporarily removed from your PC. You cannot use them in battles or send them on another expedition until you collect them.

Key rules

  • You can have only one expedition at a time.
  • Expeditions last 4, 8 or 16 hours; the timer keeps running while you are offline.
  • You cannot cancel an expedition yourself once it has started.
  • You must collect your Pokémon and rewards manually when the expedition is complete.
  • You cannot start another expedition until you have collected the previous one.
  • Make sure you have enough free PC slots before collecting your team.
  • Your team and the expedition rules are recorded when the expedition starts.

Expedition Strength (SE)

SE represents a Pokémon's expedition potential. It depends on the species' base stat total (BST), level, natural IVs, EVs and special SE-boosting held items. The SE values of the selected Pokémon are added together to produce the team's total SE.

Hyper Training does not increase the natural IVs used for the SE calculation.

How to check SE

Use the player command to see the SE of Pokémon in your current party and their combined total. The expedition selection screen also shows information such as SE, type, IVs and Shiny status.

Items that boost SE

Three special held items provide an SE bonus to the Pokémon holding them. The bonus is included when the expedition starts.

ItemBonus

Emblemat Wyprawy+10% SE
Relikt Ekspedycyjny+15% SE

All expeditions

4-hour expeditions

Type and Shiny requirements refer to the Pokémon sent on the selected expedition. Average natural IVs are calculated across the entire selected team.

Expedition rewards

Each expedition has its own reward pool. Besides everyday items and materials, you can win Mega Stones, valuable held items, cosmetics, auras and Title Scrolls.

Rare Mega Stones

Examples of rare rewards include:

  • Mewtwonite X and Mewtwonite Y
  • Charizardite X and Charizardite Y
  • Garchompite, Metagrossite and Lucarionite
  • Latiosite and Latiasite
  • Dragoninite, Gengarite and Salamencite

Each stone is available from specific expeditions.

Powerful Pokémon items

Selected expeditions can reward valuable held items such as:

  • Leftovers
  • Assault Vest
  • Choice Specs
  • Eviolite
  • Loaded Dice
  • Weakness Policy
  • Flame Orb
  • Expert Belt

These items are useful when preparing teams for tougher battles.

Cosmetics and auras

Special cosmetics and auras let you customize the appearance of your character or Pokémon. They do not provide combat stat bonuses. You can find them on these expeditions:

Title Scrolls

Some expeditions also offer Title Scrolls from Eryndor Identity. A scroll unlocks its associated title, which you can display next to your nickname in chat. Some titles are rare special rewards.

Does higher SE mean better rewards?

Yes. If your team's SE exceeds the expedition's minimum requirement, the excess can increase ordinary reward quantities and the chances of special rewards, by up to twice the base value. It does not change the list of items available on that expedition.

Quantity rewards have defined ranges; some have a minimum of zero. Each special reward is rolled independently, so a single expedition can yield several valuable prizes, one, or none.

You can check the full reward pool and chances for each expedition in its details at the NPC before sending your Pokémon.

Expeditions and Eryndor Mastery

Expeditions work with Eryndor Mastery. A Pokémon that completes an expedition and meets the requirements of its current Mastery stage may receive one expedition credit towards its current rank.

  • Mastery begins at level 100.
  • An expedition counts when it is completed, not when it starts.
  • A completed expedition may award a Pokémon only one Mastery expedition credit.
  • An expedition credit does not replace the required battles.

Collecting a completed expedition

After the timer runs out, the expedition is ready to collect. Return to the NPC, open the expedition menu, review the rewards and collect your team. Your Pokémon will return to the PC. If there are not enough free slots, clear some space first.

You do not need to be online when the expedition finishes. You can collect it later.

Practical tips

  • Check your SE before choosing an expedition — meeting the minimum does not guarantee the maximum reward bonus.
  • For average-IV requirements, focus on the whole team rather than just one exceptional Pokémon.
  • Special SE held items can help you reach the required threshold.
  • Shiny Pokémon are required on some expeditions, but do not replace the minimum SE requirement.
  • Do not send Pokémon you will need before the expedition finishes.
  • When training Mastery, send Pokémon that are already eligible to earn progress for their current rank.

chronicles-trials.title: The Trail of Trials
chronicles-trials.summary: Why visiting Trainers collect Gym Badges, and how the Trail of Trials connects Eryndor's three islands.
chronicles-trials.search: eryndor trail of trials gyms gym leaders badges visiting trainers khar-durim valoria sah'rava ferry
chronicles-trials.content:
If you arrived in Eryndor as a merchant, sailor, or ordinary traveler, chances are nobody will ask how powerful your Pokémon are.

But if you introduce yourself as a Trainer, things are different.

In Eryndor, a powerful Trainer is more than a tournament competitor.

A well-trained team of Pokémon can protect a settlement, stop a dangerous creature, help during a disaster, or turn the tide of battle faster than an entire company of ordinary warriors.

That is why newcomers who wish to be recognized as Trainers must follow the Trail of Trials.

Each of the great islands has respected Gym Leaders whom local rulers and communities have entrusted with judging visiting Trainers.

Each Leader oversees an Arena and sets a challenge of their own.

Defeat a Leader, and you earn their Badge.

One Badge says little.

A complete set means something else entirely.

It means the island's foremost Trainers have seen what you can do and decided that you are more than another stranger with a Poké Ball at your belt.

Only then will the official ferrymen allow you to continue along the Trail to the next great island.

This is not a law that applies to every resident of Eryndor.

Merchants still trade.

Envoys cross the seas.

Families visit their relatives.

The Trials concern visiting Trainers.

For the rulers of Eryndor have learned one thing:

when someone arrives in their kingdom commanding six powerful Pokémon, it is wise to know who that person really is.

On Khar-Durim, the Leaders look for strength, endurance, and determination.

On Valoria, the Trials resemble tournaments, although the royal court watches those who complete them all very closely.

On the divided island of Sah'Rava, there is no single crown able to set rules for everyone. There, the various peoples and noble houses entrust their Trials to Leaders of their own.

Their Badges may look different.

Their rules may differ.

But their meaning remains the same.

You have crossed our island. We have come to know you. You may continue onward.

Completing the Trail does not mean you must serve a king.

No one will pin a royal crest to your chest merely because you command Pokémon well.

But your name will be remembered.

And in Eryndor, you never know when a king, a lord, a clan chief, or an ordinary village might need the help of someone who has already proved themselves worthy of notice.

An old saying is passed among Trainers:

“First, come to know the island on which you stand. Only then ask the sea to show you the next.”

That is the Trail of Trials.

Journey Through the Chronicles

ascension.title: Eryndor Awakening
ascension.summary: Awakening moves after level 105, Relics, Triumph Spheres, Miner's Seals, Fortune's Signs, Tears of the Deep and crafting recipes.
ascension.search: awakening ascension relic triumph sphere 700 victories miner seal diamond emerald netherite fortune sign casino tokens tear of the deep fishing mastery level 105 moves
ascension.content:
Reaching level 105 does not have to be the end of a Pokémon's growth. Awakening lets you go beyond a Pokémon's natural move pool and teach it powerful moves it normally could not learn.

Awakening is the next stage of progression after Eryndor Mastery. It does not increase a Pokémon's stats or maximum level. Instead, it opens up entirely new possibilities in battle.

What is Awakening?

Any Pokémon that has reached level 105 can undergo the Awakening ritual.

During the ritual, you use an Awakening Relic to permanently unlock one chosen move from a special pool available on Eryndor.

Key rules:

  • Awakening is available to level 105 Pokémon.
  • One Awakening Relic unlocks one new move.
  • The unlocked move is permanently tied to that particular Pokémon.
  • You can unlock more than one move on the same Pokémon.
  • Once a move has been unlocked, you can assign it again later at no additional cost.
  • A Pokémon can still have at most four active moves at a time.

The system includes 73 special moves, ranging from powerful attacks to useful support moves.

Not every move will suit every Pokémon. How you use your team's new possibilities is up to you.

How to Awaken a Pokémon

  1. Raise the chosen Pokémon to level 105.
  2. Obtain an Awakening Relic.
  3. Open the Awakening panel and select a Pokémon from your party.
  4. Choose the move you want to unlock permanently.
  5. Confirm the ritual. One Relic will be consumed.

The Pokémon remembers the unlock. Even if you replace that move later, you can still teach it again.

In the Awakening panel, you can also manage moves you have already unlocked and assign them to your active moveset. Moves cannot be changed during battle.

How do you obtain an Awakening Relic?

An Awakening Relic is not an ordinary item earned by defeating a single opponent.

To craft one, combine four elements obtained through different activities across Eryndor.

ElementHow to obtain it
Triumph Sphere (charged)Expeditions into adventure areas and Dungeons, then defeating wild Pokémon
Miner's SealCrafting with valuable resources
Fortune's SignCasino Shop — 100 tokens
Tear of the DeepRare treasure reward from Pixelmon Fishing

Each element represents a different kind of effort: victories in battle, riches mined from the earth, luck, and patience while fishing.

Triumph Sphere

The Triumph Sphere is a special item that can be obtained as a rare reward from adventure runs and Dungeons.

The Sphere starts empty. To prepare it for Relic crafting, you must fill it with the energy of victories.

Charging one Sphere requires 700 victories over wild Pokémon.

  • The Sphere charges whenever you defeat a wild Pokémon while carrying it in your inventory.
  • Each qualifying victory adds 1 point.
  • You can check progress in the item's description.
  • You can charge several Spheres at the same time.
  • Upon reaching 700 points, it becomes a Triumph Sphere (charged).

Simply catching Pokémon or winning Trainer battles does not replace the required victories against wild Pokémon.

A fully charged Sphere is ready to be used in Awakening Relic crafting.

Miner's Seal

The Miner's Seal is a component of the Relic that you can craft at a crafting table.

Ingredients: 4 Diamond Blocks, 4 Emerald Blocks, and 1 Netherite Ingot.

Miner's Seal crafting — 3×3 layout

Diamond BlockEmerald BlockDiamond Block
Emerald BlockNetherite IngotEmerald Block
Diamond BlockEmerald BlockDiamond Block

The arrangement matters — place the ingredients exactly as shown. The recipe produces one Miner's Seal.

Fortune's Sign

You can purchase Fortune's Sign in the Eryndor Casino Shop for 100 Casino Tokens.

You earn tokens by playing 777 slot machines and blackjack. Fortune's Sign is one way to turn your casino winnings into further Pokémon progression.

Tear of the Deep

Tear of the Deep is a rare treasure associated with Pixelmon Fishing.

Use Eryndor's special fishing rod and look for treasures during fishing trips to find one.

It is not an ordinary fish or cooking ingredient, but a special item used to craft an Awakening Relic.

For more information about the fishing rod, fishing minigame and treasures, see the Pixelmon Fishing guide.

Crafting an Awakening Relic

Once you have collected all four elements, combine them at a crafting table:

  • 1 × charged Triumph Sphere
  • 1 × Miner's Seal
  • 1 × Fortune's Sign
  • 1 × Tear of the Deep

Result: 1 × Awakening Relic.

You can place the ingredients in any slots on the crafting grid — their order does not matter.

The Relic is consumed when you unlock a new move.

Can you Awaken the same Pokémon more than once?

Yes! Each additional Relic lets you unlock another eligible move. Awakening is not limited to a single ritual per Pokémon.

Most importantly, every unlocked move remains available to that Pokémon permanently.

You can experiment with different movesets, adapt to opponents and adjust your strategy without crafting more Relics for moves you have already unlocked.

Awakening does not replace training, good stats or thoughtful team building.

It offers something different: a chance to create a Pokémon whose capabilities cannot be judged by its species alone.

trade-chain.title: Trade Chain — Pokémon Trading Paths
trade-chain.summary: Discover special Pokémon trades, rare rewards and species excluded from natural spawning — without spoiling the trading chains.

trade-chain.content:
Not every Pokémon in Eryndor can be found in the wild. Some require more than patient searching, the right biome, or a lucky encounter.

Trade Chain is a special trading system that lets you obtain rare and exceptional Pokémon by discovering new trading opportunities.

What is Trade Chain?

Throughout Eryndor, you will encounter Pokémon traders who offer exchanges unavailable in standard Pixelmon.

Instead of buying Pokémon with money, you must find the right creatures and trade them for others.

Some transactions open up further opportunities. Others let you obtain Pokémon you will never encounter while exploring the world normally.

Key rules:

  • Some Pokémon have been completely removed from natural spawning.
  • To obtain exceptional Pokémon, you need to discover available trades.
  • Trade Chain includes ordinary Pokémon as well as Legendary, Mythical, and Paradox Pokémon.
  • Not every trade leads to the same destination.
  • It is worth carefully examining the offers of the traders you meet.

Discovering exchanges is part of the adventure. You will not find the order of trades or the solutions to any chains in this guide.

Which Pokémon can you obtain?

Exceptional Pokémon

Trade Chain lets you obtain 12 particularly valuable Pokémon:

DragapultDragoniteGarchomp
VolcaronaSalamenceMetagross
HydreigonToxapexSnorlax
FerrothornGholdengoTyranitar

Many of these Pokémon are powerful in battle and make valuable additions to a team.

Legendary and Mythical Pokémon

There are also trades leading to six exceptional Pokémon:

EnteiSuicune
RaikouKeldeo
MagearnaTing-Lu

Obtaining them requires discovering the appropriate trading path.

Paradox Pokémon

Trade Chain also lets you obtain eight Paradox Pokémon:

Great TuskIron Hands
Slither WingIron Jugulis
Scream TailIron Thorns
Roaring MoonIron Valiant

Paradox Pokémon are different from ordinary species and do not spawn naturally in Eryndor.

Pokémon removed from natural spawning

To preserve the importance of the trading system, certain Pokémon and forms no longer appear naturally in Eryndor.

The following list covers both potential rewards and other species connected to the system.

This list is alphabetical; it does not reveal the order of any trades.

Ordinary Pokémon and forms

A–D

Alcremie, Annihilape, Bagon, Basculegion, Beautifly, Beldum, Bisharp, Braviary (including Hisuian form), Cascoon, Deino, Dragapult, Dragonair, Dragonite, Drakloak, Dratini, Dreepy, Dudunsparce (both forms), Dustox.

  • Entei

  • Ting-Lu

Paradox Pokémon

Not every Pokémon listed in this table is a Trade Chain reward. Some belong to other special ways of obtaining Pokémon.

Is Trade Chain the only way to obtain these Pokémon?

Not spawning naturally does not always mean a Pokémon is available exclusively through Trade Chain.

Eryndor also features special reward systems, events, and crates that can grant selected exceptional Pokémon.

For example, Snorlax is connected to Trade Chain but can also appear as a special Event Crate reward.

The important distinction is between encountering a Pokémon naturally and obtaining one through a controlled reward source.

Discover the trades

Trade Chain was created to make acquiring certain Pokémon an adventure in its own right.

You do not need to uncover every possibility at once. Talk to the traders you encounter, study their offers, and discover the paths available to you over time.

A Pokémon that does not seem especially valuable at first glance may turn out to matter far more than you initially thought.

In Eryndor, not every treasure waits inside a chest. Sometimes it waits on the other side of a trade.

auras.summary: Cosmetic auras, the Accessories aura slot, 17 reward auras, and Fisher and Mushroom Aura earned through their Atlases.

auras.content:
Eryndor Auras are special visual effects that surround your character. Flames, magical particles, orbiting symbols and glowing trails let you give your adventurer a distinctive look.

Auras are collectible cosmetic rewards. They do not increase damage, Pokémon stats or your chances of finding Shiny Pokémon. They are a way to personalize your appearance and show off the decorations you have earned.

How do you equip an aura?

  1. Obtain the item representing the aura you want.
  2. Open Options → Controls → Key Binds and find the shortcut for the cosmetics / accessories menu (Accessories).
  3. Assign an available key and press it to open the separate cosmetics window.
  4. Place the item in the dedicated Aura slot.
  5. The particle effect will appear around your character.

Important: Pixelmon replaces Minecraft's regular inventory screen with its own interface. Therefore, the cosmetics menu cannot be opened through the normal inventory screen: use your assigned shortcut instead.

An aura uses its own accessory slot. You do not need to hold it or replace your armor. To change your appearance, simply replace the aura item in that slot.

Where can you obtain auras?

Eryndor features 17 selected auras distributed across activities, reward crates and shops. Some have more than one source.

Each source has its own rules. For example, crates require suitable keys, while shops use currencies earned through other activities. This table tells you where to look for each aura without disclosing drop probabilities.

Two auras for completing Atlases

There are also two exceptional auras tied to exploring the world. They are separate from the collection of 17 auras available through crates, shops and other rewards.

  • Fisher Aura — a reward for completing the Fish Atlas in Pixelmon Fishing.
  • Mushroom Aura — a reward for completing the Mushroom Atlas in Mushroom Foraging.

To earn these decorations, you must discover every species required by the relevant Atlas. Where and how to find them is part of the adventure.

Auras and Eryndor Mastery

It is important to distinguish auras equipped by players from the particle effects associated with Pokémon progressing through Eryndor Mastery.

Mastery effects appear around Pokémon and reflect their M1–M5 ranks. They do not require an item in the Aura accessory slot.

The Mastery Aura in the table above, however, is a separate character cosmetic obtainable as an Expedition reward. It is not the same as the automatic Mastery effects on Pokémon.

Similarly, the name Shimmering Aura describes a visual effect. It does not turn a Pokémon Shiny or improve your chances of finding one.

How do you hide aura particles?

If you prefer fewer particles on your screen, you can toggle aura visibility with this command:

/auras particles toggle

Run the command again to restore the effects. This changes what you see — it does not remove another player's aura or unequip your own item.

Mastery effects have their own visibility settings, described in the Eryndor Mastery guide.
